evidence: Compared word by word with SOURCE.txt. Draft: 'Conscious agreement, unconscious receptivity, emotional compliance, legal and ethical consent - can people have their minds influenced without the conscious agreement of their adult self?' Words it replaces: the same four-item list as a fragment, then 'Can people have their minds influenced without conscious agreement of their adult self?'. The only differences from those words are the full stop between list and question becoming ' - ', 'Can' becoming 'can', and 'the' added before 'conscious agreement' (part of Emulate's version; the_change does not mention it; it changes no meaning). All four of his kinds are present in his wording and order, 'their adult self' and 'people ... their minds influenced' are kept, and nothing is added: no claim, condition, person, number or named entity. The change does what the_change says (the four kinds joined to the question with a dash), and the_change does not claim to put anything back, so nothing promised is missing; in any case all four kinds are there. Against his published lines ('Conscious agreement is one thing. Unconscious receptivity is another. Emotional compliance is another. Legal and ethical consent is another. A mind can be influenced without the adult self having clearly chosen the influence.'): the draft does not say outright that the four are different things, and it puts the influence point as a question with 'conscious agreement' where he has 'clearly chosen'. I checked, and that is already how the words it replaces read, so this change neither adds nor removes strength; the paragraph before it (influence without the conscious mind, FTC, OECD) supplies the yes and the Silva line after it carries the point on, so the question still works as the rhetorical one it was. Reads right in context: 24 words; ' - ' is the same spaced hyphen the previous paragraph already uses ('dark patterns' - designs used to trick...); no stray space before the question mark; no typos. Tells: I went through T01 to T29 and C01 to C04 on the literal draft in its context and found none actually happening. Closest calls, all judged absent: T12 (a four-part list, but they are his published four in his order and the replaced text already listed them, so it is not a list made for balance); T21 (one sentence of list plus question, but it does one argumentative job, the question); T24 (a question, but it is not answered at once or for suspense: the paragraph before already states the claim and this turns it to consent, and the Silva line after is a new step); T26 ('conscious agreement' appears twice in the sentence, but it is the list's first item and the question's object, so the repetition ties them together); T25 (the dash follows a real list of four, so it is not a colon reveal). Linter: 'B4/E15 list or packed sentence' accepted: the list is his own four, the replaced text already listed it, the join adds no extra job and the sentence is only 24 words. 'D9 follows the source order' accepted: it is one sentence that follows the order of the words it replaces because it is those words; I checked T13 and T09 and there is nothing for them to flag in a one-sentence paragraph when the rest of the section is not touched by this change.
